steps.tx: **Neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus** or NPSLE encompasses 19 case definitions standardized by the ACR. Diffuse neuropsychiatric syndromes such as lupus psychosis and severe cognitive dysfunction correlate strongly with **anti-ribosomal P antibodies**, while active psychosis is accompanied by CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis and elevated IgG index.
steps.say: Neuropsychiatric lupus encompasses 19 ACR definitions. Diffuse psychiatric manifestations and lupus psychosis link with anti-ribosomal P antibodies and elevated CSF IgG index.

rows: Lupus psychosis, acute confusional state, cognitive decline
Anti-ribosomal P antibodies, elevated CSF IgG index
Abnormal electromyography and nerve conduction studies

steps.tx: **Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder** or NMOSD co-occurs with systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjogren disease. Pathogenic IgG antibodies target **aquaporin-4** water channels on astrocyte foot processes, causing extensive astrocytopathy that produces **longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis** spanning **3 or more vertebral segments** on MRI.
steps.say: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder co-occurs with SLE and Sjogren disease. Anti-aquaporin-4 antibodies attack astrocytes, causing transverse myelitis spanning 3 or more vertebral segments.

vis.alt: Aquaporin-4 targeting and longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis in NMOSD
vis.caption: Pathogenic anti-AQP4 antibodies target astrocytes, causing extensive transverse myelitis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Primary angiitis of the central nervous system** or PACNS is restricted to parenchymal and leptomeningeal arteries under 500 micrometres. Definitive diagnosis requires high-resolution vessel wall MRI or **stereotactic brain-leptomeningeal biopsy** demonstrating transmural granulomatous, lymphocytic, or necrotizing arteritis, carefully excluding reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome.
steps.say: Primary CNS angiitis is restricted to small cerebral arteries. High-resolution vessel wall MRI and brain-leptomeningeal biopsy provide definitive histopathologic confirmation.

nodes.label: Subacute cognitive decline, persistent headache, recurrent strokes
High-resolution vessel wall MRI showing concentric arterial enhancement
Targeted stereotactic brain and leptomeningeal biopsy confirms transmural arteritis

steps.tx: **Mononeuritis multiplex** is an asymmetric, asynchronous axonal neuropathy involving **2 or more non-contiguous nerve trunks**. It is the neurological hallmark of necrotizing systemic vasculitides including polyarteritis nodosa, EGPA, and microscopic polyangiitis, caused by ischemic infarction of nerve fascicles from **vasculitis of epineurial arterioles**.
steps.say: Mononeuritis multiplex affects two or more non-contiguous peripheral nerve trunks. It represents the neurologic hallmark of necrotizing vasculitis caused by epineurial arteritis.

left.title: Mononeuritis multiplex
points: Hallmark of PAN, EGPA, and MPA vasculitis

right.title: Distal symmetric polyneuropathy
points: Common in diabetes and systemic sclerosis

steps.tx: The image pairs the **ulnar nerve** in the arm with the **common peroneal nerve** at the knee to show two separate trunks hit at different sites. One inset shows **epineurial arteritis** with vessel wall inflammation while the other shows patchy axonal loss. This pattern defines mononeuritis multiplex and points to small vessel vasculitis starving single nerves rather than one diffuse polyneuropathy.
steps.say: Here you see two far apart nerves picked out, one in the arm and one near the knee. The close up views show an inflamed small vessel in the nerve cover and loss of axons downstream. Hitting separate named trunks at different times is the clue. It favors vasculitis cutting off single nerves over a single diffuse process affecting all feet and hands together.

vis.alt: Paired views of the ulnar nerve in the arm and the common peroneal nerve at the knee with insets showing vessel inflammation and axonal loss.
vis.caption: Two separate nerve trunks hit by small vessel inflammation, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Neuro-Behcet disease** manifests with parenchymal involvement in **80 percent** of cases, presenting as a brainstem-diencephalic syndrome with pyramidal and cerebellar signs. Non-parenchymal disease in **20 percent** presents as **cerebral venous sinus thrombosis**. Parenchymal neuro-Behcet requires emergency pulse methylprednisolone combined with **anti-TNF therapy** or azathioprine.
steps.say: Neuro-Behcet disease presents with parenchymal brainstem involvement in 80 percent and cerebral venous thrombosis in 20 percent. Parenchymal disease responds to steroids and anti-TNF therapy.

rows: 80%; brainstem diencephalic syndrome, ataxia, pyramidal signs
High-dose glucocorticoids plus infliximab or azathioprine
20%; dural venous sinus thrombosis, intracranial hypertension
Short-course glucocorticoids and systemic therapeutic anticoagulation

steps.tx: **Neurosarcoidosis** exhibits a strong predilection for the skull base and basilar leptomeninges. Common manifestations include **cranial neuropathy VII** presenting with unilateral or bilateral Bell palsy in **50 percent**, hypothalamic-pituitary granulomas causing diabetes insipidus, and thick nodular leptomeningeal enhancement on post-contrast brain MRI.
steps.say: Neurosarcoidosis has a predilection for basal meninges. It causes facial nerve palsy in 50 percent of cases, diabetes insipidus, and nodular leptomeningeal enhancement on MRI.

nodes.label: Non-caseating granulomatous infiltration of basal leptomeninges
Unilateral or bilateral cranial nerve VII palsy in 50 percent
Hypothalamic-pituitary axis granulomas causing central diabetes insipidus

steps.tx: **Hypertrophic pachymeningitis** is marked by diffuse, fibrotic thickening of the cranial or spinal dura mater with prominent contrast enhancement sparing the underlying leptomeninges. It is a characteristic neuro-rheumatologic complication of **IgG4-related disease** and ANCA-associated vasculitis, particularly **PR3-positive GPA**, often causing severe persistent headaches and cranial nerve palsies.
steps.say: Hypertrophic pachymeningitis is marked by diffuse dural thickening with contrast enhancement. It is a characteristic complication of IgG4-related disease and PR3-positive GPA.

left.title: IgG4-related pachymeningitis
points: Rapid response to corticosteroids and rituximab

steps.tx: In rheumatoid arthritis, cervical spine involvement produces **atlantoaxial subluxation** when synovial pannus erodes the transverse odontoid ligament. Instability is defined on flexion-extension radiographs by an **anterior atlanto-dens interval exceeding 3 mm** in adults; an anterior interval **greater than 9 mm** indicates impending medullary compression requiring surgical stabilization.
steps.say: Synovial pannus erodes the transverse odontoid ligament in rheumatoid arthritis, causing atlantoaxial subluxation. An anterior interval over 9 mm warns of impending cord compression.

rows: Urgent surgical posterior cervical fusion indicated
